ledger.contains: Employment Ministry report (April 2015, 105 pp.) on the first year of the Ley 14/2013 mobility section (30 Sep 2013 - 31 Dec 2014). In scope and recorded: investor grants by route (Cuadro 1 and 3, counts existing; route shares of grants and of investment added; business-project investment EUR 39,533,600 as estimate); real-estate grants and investment by nationality (Cuadro 4: euros, 'Resto' and both percentage columns added); average real-estate investment for Russian, Chinese, Venezuelan and US investors; investments above EUR 1 million (Russia 33, China 6); grants by province (Cuadro 5) and investment for Barcelona, Málaga, Madrid; financial-asset grants and investment by nationality (Cuadro 6) and business-project grants by nationality (Cuadro 7); 18 favourable general-interest reports; estimated direct jobs (Cuadro 18: real estate 1,127, financial 114, business projects 374); investors' 17% share of all Ley 14/2013 grants; fees of the Orden ESSI/1571/2014 (EUR 70.40 initial, 75.60 renewal); statutory deadlines. All tables add up to their printed totals. Out of scope: entrepreneurs, highly-qualified, researchers, intra-company transfers, family members of all categories (2,461), the EUR 694 million and 12,685 jobs totals for all categories, the press section (NYT etc. figures cover all categories), conclusions restating the same totals, and the annex comparing Ley 14/2013 with the general regime (rules already recorded from the BOE). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

ledger.contains: MAC report 'Tier 1 (Investor) route: investment thresholds and economic benefits' (Feb 2014, 108 pp.). Ch. 1: call for evidence (25 organisation and 12 individual submissions; Annex A says 10 individuals; ~200 investors contacted; calls with 4 investors). Ch. 2: rules and history (thresholds, settlement and citizenship periods, Table 2.2), Home Office grant data: Table 2.3 out-of-country and in-country grants (main/dependants) YE 2009 Q3-2013 Q3, Table 2.4 top-10 nationalities 2008 Q3-2013 Q3, refusals, in-country cumulative grants, Table 2.5 previous visa types 2011-2012, age shares and average ages, dependant ratios. Ch. 3: investment of about GBP 500m a year, Table 3.1 living expenditure, Table 3.2 spending and taxes per investor, professional-services fees, 638 dependant children, partner survey shares. Ch. 4: 90-100% invest the minimum, Tables 4.1-4.3 on other countries. Ch. 5-6: inflation-uplift thresholds (GBP 1.9m/2m/1.8m), recommendations (GBP 2m minimum; auction of about 100 premium visas with a GBP 2.5m reserve incl. a GBP 500,000 gift; 90-day residence), Table 6.1. Added 97 observations (all remaining UK route numbers above, with Table 2.4 and Table 3.2 parts checked against their printed totals) and 5 rule rows; 29 rows were already in the data. Single-case anecdotes (one investor's GBP 23,000 school fees, a client spending GBP 14m on property, a GBP 50m purchase) and macro context (deficit, gilt market size, ISC pupil numbers, London property inflows, gilt yields) are not programme statistics and are not recorded. The MAC recommendations and the Mishcon de Reya GBP 1-2bn claim for a hypothetical GBP 20m route are proposals, not recorded as numbers (the recommendation is covered by the existing event). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).
